slides.0.title: Wine types, producer structure and still wines
slides.0.subtitle: NV, Vintage, RM/NM/CM and Coteaux Champenois
slides.1.title: Types of Champagne
slides.1.highlights.0.title: NV and Vintage
slides.1.highlights.0.content: NV can blend several years; Vintage uses grapes of one year only, with no reserve wine, at most 80% of an operator's wine of that year and at least 36 months before release
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Blanc de Blancs and Blanc de Noirs
slides.1.highlights.1.content: The specification describes whites as blends of white and black grapes, only white grapes (Blanc de Blancs) or only black grapes (Blanc de Noirs)
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Rosé
slides.1.highlights.2.content: The specification allows direct pressing, maceration or saignée, or blending white and red before tirage; blending is a hallmark of Champagne rosé (about 5–20% red)
slides.1.highlights.3.title: Prestige cuvée
slides.1.highlights.3.content: A market term for a house's top wine; it does not appear in the INAO specification and has no legal definition; such wines usually come from better plots and age longer
slides.1.content: Law defines NV, Vintage, colour and grape make-up; Prestige is brand language.
slides.2.title: Producer structure
slides.2.highlights.0.title: Three kinds of operator
slides.2.highlights.0.content: About 16,460 growers, 410 houses and 120 cooperatives (Comité Champagne key figures, 2025 edition); the 2023 edition said 16,200/370/130 and 2024 said 16,300/390/125, so the numbers move and are not tested
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Label codes
slides.2.highlights.1.content: NM (négociant-manipulant, house), RM (récoltant-manipulant, grower-producer), CM (cooperative), RC (cooperative-member seller), SR (growers' company), ND (distributor) and MA (buyer's own brand)
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Who ships what
slides.2.highlights.2.content: About 266.1 million bottles in 2025, 191.9 million from houses and 74.2 million from cooperatives and growers (Comité Champagne 2025), so houses ship about 72% (our calculation)
slides.2.highlights.3.title: Who owns the grapes
slides.2.highlights.3.content: Growers own close to 90% of the vineyard and most houses grow under half of what they need, so they buy grapes from growers (Academie du Vin, 2019 data), the structural source of price and yield bargaining
slides.2.content: Codes and counts change; the logic of who makes and who sells is what matters.
slides.3.title: Comité Champagne and yield decisions
slides.3.highlights.0.title: A two-sided body
slides.3.highlights.0.content: The Comité Interprofessionnel du Vin de Champagne was created by the law of 12 April 1941 and joins the growers' SGV (founded 1904) and the houses' UMC (founded 1882) (INAO specification)
slides.3.highlights.1.title: The annual summer decision
slides.3.highlights.1.content: The Comité sets the marketable yield each summer, about six to eight weeks before harvest, weighing sales, stocks, expected quality and the market
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Recent figures
slides.3.highlights.2.content: 12,000 in 2022, 11,400 in 2023, 10,000 in 2024, 9,000 in 2025 and 8,800 kg/ha in 2026 (press reports; examples only, not tested)
slides.3.highlights.3.title: A tug of interests
slides.3.highlights.3.content: Growers are paid by the kilo and lean towards higher yields; houses sell the wine and fear a glut that depresses prices (Academie du Vin). This tension is central to MW essays and returns in Level 3
slides.3.content: Yield decisions are negotiated inside the industry, not a unilateral government order.
slides.4.title: Still wines and by-products
slides.4.highlights.0.title: Coteaux Champenois
slides.4.highlights.0.content: Still white, rosé and red; at least 9% natural alcohol and 143 g/L sugar in the grapes; the same area as Champagne; the newer draft variety list includes Chardonnay Rosé
slides.4.highlights.1.title: Rosé des Riceys
slides.4.highlights.1.content: A still rosé AOC (1947) from Pinot Noir only, made by whole-bunch semi-carbonic maceration with at least 10% natural alcohol (INAO 2026 draft), about 50,000–150,000 bottles a year
slides.4.highlights.2.title: Ratafia and spirits
slides.4.highlights.2.content: Ratafia de Champagne gained PGI status in 2015, made from Champagne grape juice fortified with grape-based spirit; Marc and Fine (Marc de Champagne, Fine de la Marne) are regional spirits not individually verified here and not tested
slides.4.highlights.3.title: Where rebêches go
slides.4.highlights.3.content: Rebêches must be sent for distillation before 15 December of the year after harvest, although the specification also lets them be used to make a liqueur inside the area
slides.4.content: Still wines and by-products are tiny; exams focus on names, varieties and rules.
slides.5.componentProps.slide.title: 🧠 Knowledge check
What does the label code RM stand for?
B. A grower who makes and sells their own Champagne
RM is récoltant-manipulant, a grower-producer; houses are NM and cooperatives CM.
What share of an operator's wine of the year may be presented as Vintage under the specification?
Specification: vintage wines may not exceed 80% of the year's wine, keeping room for reserve wines.
Which statement about Rosé des Riceys is correct?
A. A still rosé from Pinot Noir only
B. A sparkling rosé from Meunier
INAO specification: Pinot Noir only, still rosé, limited to Les Riceys.
